method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the family member of the person who died (or another person with a sufficient interest), with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05; dates, the regulative vocabulary and the schedule 2 family member in one shared module (built-in date functions, no daydate), then four rule modules (reporting and investigating; the autopsy and the body; the inquest and findings; documents and physical evidence), each exported question calling a rule defined beside it, and a worked-case file for each; two regulative rules (ss 24(6), 30(3)) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Coroners Act 2003 (Qld), act-2003-013, the version in force from 2026-10-29 (current on 2026-11-06), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/act-2003-013.txt (text sha256 6b85fcaefc15d55b7f51a33def8b96803e923e9e83f14348bf9b12c636fbd853 per its meta.json); converted from the Queensland Legislation HTML view; no instrument brought in (none sets a number the encoded sections use)

seat: the family member of the person who died, or another person with a sufficient interest in the death (for s 7 any person who becomes aware of the death; for ss 59-62 the owner of property held as evidence, including the deceased's personal representative)

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run <file> for each of the nine .l4 files, from this folder, at most two at a time
checks.result: 221 assertions written, 221 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: Part 2 and part 3 as the family meets them, with s 95 and the schedule 2 family member. In: ss 7(1)-(3), (7), 8, 8A, 9, 10, 10AA; 11(2)-(4), (7), 11AAA(1), (3), (4), 11A, 12(1); 19(1), (5), (6), 20(3)-(5), 21(3)-(5), 23A, 24(4)-(9), 26(2)(f), (3), (4); 27, 28(1), 29, 30, 36, 39, 45(3)-(5), 46(1)-(3), 46A, 50, 51(2); 52, 54(1)-(4), (7), 55, 56, 57; 59-62A; 95; sch 2 family member, not reasonably available. Out: part 1, ss 98, 99, part 6 (machinery and transition); part 4 (the court and coroners), part 4A (the review board); ss 92-94, 97; duties between officials (ss 7(4)-(6), 10A, 14, 15, 18, 18A, 25(4)-(6), 47, 47A, 48, 49, 54AA-54C, 58, 63, 63A); s 11AA (preliminary examinations, could be added as s 19(5) was); the coroner's own powers and other release paths (ss 12(2)-(4), 13, 19(2)-(4), (7)-(9), 20(1), (2), (6)-(8), 21(1), (2), 23, 24(1)-(3), (10), 26(1), (2)(a)-(e), (6)); witnesses, doctors and the public (ss 16, 17, 17A, 22, 24A, 25(1)-(3), 26(5), 37, 41: other seats); inquest procedure (ss 31-35, 38, 40, 42-44); ss 45(1), (2), (6), (7), 46(4), 50A, 50B, 51(1), (3), 53, 54(5), (6), 96. Reasons in NOTES.md.
